01 / THE SCENE

Three heroes. One giant threat.

Soldiers and heroes share the supplied Explosive LLC low-poly character and weighted rig, with distinct faction and hero colors. Rift Warden teleports between rooftops through golden-green portals. His stationary attack portals last five seconds and fire larger, sparkling projectiles at four shots per second; when friendly armor or infantry is threatened, he opens paired ground portals to evacuate them. Volt Rush fights alongside the armies under CPU control, sometimes sprinting up buildings to fire lightning from the rooftops. Take over to sprint through the streets, run up buildings and fire electricity; exiting hands control back to him. His short rescue dash carries nearby allies forward in a burst of lightning; the CPU tries it when nearby allies face incoming projectiles. Violet Sentinel circles a 21-metre robot, charging purple force orbs between his hands. When helicopters are threatened, he races into the beam’s path and raises a massive energy barrier. Both divisions turn their tanks, helicopters, and rifle squads against its armor. The Walker gathers energy into its arm cannon, looks toward its locked firing target, then unleashes a seven-second plasma beam. Red warning lines preview the beam’s path and sweep while it charges. After the beam, its raised shoulder pod flashes a warning before launching six slow, smoke-trailing missiles. The opposite shoulder carries a large plasma cannon elevated at 45 degrees. It lobs glowing plasma balls high above the city; large ground targets count down to impact. Solara Frost rides a growing ice path, attacks with fireballs and raises ice domes to intercept incoming plasma over tanks and soldiers. Volt Rush can dash nearby allies clear. Choose Heroes to change your active team. After a five-second opening delay, the Walker cycles beam cannon, missiles, then plasma cannon, with a five-second pause between attacks. The plasma cannon stays forward-facing as the robot turns to aim. Violet Sentinel fires slower charged purple interception orbs between shield rescues while CPU-controlled Volt Rush shoots missiles down with lightning.

02 / THE DESTRUCTION

Damage with weight.

Shells, rockets, and rifle fire wear down the Walker’s armor. Its damaged reactor smokes; when it fails, the robot buckles and breaks into falling rigid-body components. Buildings are 30% tougher and take 90% less damage from army, player and superhero attacks. The robot’s weapons deal full building damage. Weapon hits progressively blacken damaged panels before they fracture and collapse.

03 / THE LIMITS

A physics study.

Pre-segmented structures with simplified support rules, not engineering-grade concrete fracture. Active debris is capped for performance.

CROSSFIRE / AN OBSERVATIONAL EXPERIMENTTechnical notes ↗

Observe or join the battle.

Civilian evacuation: choose Civilian evacuation in the Scene menu. Two opposite-corner subway entrances alternate 12-person groups every 30 seconds. Each group runs and turns together in a compact formation. Protect civilians as they reach the Chinook. A three-drone squad arrives from the extended outer boulevard with the second civilian wave and advances toward the helicopter. Groups follow streets to the marked landing zone and board automatically. Helicopters approach, land, wait up to 30 seconds, depart with a full group or when the window ends, and are replaced after escaping or being destroyed; passengers count as safe when the aircraft leaves the city. Use the Chinook landing-zone camera to watch boarding. If the helicopter is lost, rebuild to retry. City battle remains available in the same menu.

Volt Rush: running and wall-running build static charge from actual distance. A full-speed run fills the 100-point meter in about six seconds. Pressing FIRE starts lightning immediately. Hold it for a continuous beam that drains 25 charge per second; a full bar lasts four seconds while stationary, and running recharge extends it. Release FIRE to stop. There is no attack cooldown or rearm delay. If the bar empties, keep holding FIRE and it resumes immediately when running generates charge. Charge does not decay while idle; movement, jumping and rescue DASH remain free. The CPU also runs to recharge. He patrols, runs up buildings and pauses on rooftops to fire lightning at the robot under CPU control. Choose Volt Rush escort to watch, or Play Volt Rush for a third-person hero. WASD moves, Shift boosts, moving the locked mouse turns the camera, hold left-click or F to sustain electricity while running, and Space jumps. E turns Volt into a short electric wave, converting and carrying friendly tanks and soldiers within five metres forward by up to ten metres. It recharges in five seconds and stops at obstacles or ledges. Use DASH on a phone. On a phone, the left stick moves forward, back and sideways relative to your view. The camera follows your running turns. Drag the scene to look around; manual looking and firing take priority. BOOST toggles super speed. JUMP, rescue DASH and FIRE are grouped above the movement stick on the left. Press FIRE for instant lightning, then keep holding to sustain it while charge remains. The player beam has no shot cooldown. You can move and fire together with separate fingers, and drag the open scene to aim. Hold forward into a facade to climb, then crest onto the roof. Boosted airborne impacts latch immediately into an upward wall run, including angled or sideways approaches. Keep boosting and moving to climb; steer away or jump to leave. Glancing contact slides along walls. Pull back or jump to leave a wall; the view stays upright while climbing. Releasing movement on a wall makes him lose grip and fall. A short jump buffer and edge grace help with rooftop jumps, and descending near a roof edge can catch the lip. The ⚙ button adjusts look sensitivity, beam aim assistance and hero sounds. Light aim assistance on desktop and mobile helps electricity catch visible missiles and robot armor just beside the reticle. It adjusts the beam without turning your camera. Direct hits and manual weak-point shots take priority; switch it off in the hero settings for fully manual aiming. Rescues count when a real hostile blast misses an ally you dashed out of its path. He follows slopes and settled rubble and cannot fly. Exit hero or Escape returns to observation and hands him back to CPU control.

Solara Frost: select her from the Heroes menu. Her anatomical right side is fire; her left side is ice. She surfs a growing ice path, uses tracking fireballs to shoot down incoming missiles, and builds ice domes over threatened soldiers and tanks. Each dome grows from a ground ring to a closed crown over 2.6 seconds. Formed ice physically intercepts plasma balls before they can damage the ground. Choose Solara Frost escort to follow her.

Hero selection: use Heroes in the header to choose up to three defenders. Deploying a different team rebuilds the battle. Volt Rush supports player control; the other heroes act automatically. Your team is saved in this browser.

Rift Warden: he joins Volt Rush and Violet Sentinel in the default team. choose his escort camera to watch him teleport. His stationary portals last five seconds and fire larger, sparkling projectiles at four shots per second. A small traveling trace connects each teleport’s source and destination. His large entrance/exit pair lasts twelve seconds, repositions nearby civilians, tanks and soldiers, and redirects physical projectiles that cross the entrance. His personal teleport remains a separate ability.

Violet Sentinel attacks the robot with charged purple force orbs and rushes to protect helicopters with an energy barrier. Choose Hero escort to follow him. The barrier physically stops beam damage while it holds.

Siege Walker weak points: shoot the four glowing cores. Amber cores are damaged; the final core flashes pink and waits until you choose to destroy it. CPU allies cannot break that last core. Completing a set deals 8% of maximum health, interrupts the current weapon and staggers the Walker for five seconds. A new set forms twelve seconds after the stagger ends. Weak points require direct hits; aim assistance continues targeting armor and missiles.

Lightning wave: E or touch DASH converts Volt into a moving wave of electricity. Nearby soldiers, tanks and civilians join it, including allies touched farther along its route. Their bodies disappear during transit and reform in safe spaces near the endpoint. The wave travels ten metres with a five-second cooldown and costs no charge. Hold a movement direction to dash that way; otherwise it follows your view. Solid obstacles and rooftop edges stop it safely.

Eye bolts: between heavy attacks, the robot charges red eye sights and fires three paired energy shots at Volt Rush. Change direction after the sights lock, dash aside, or use buildings as cover.

Plasma artillery: the opposite shoulder cannon fires high-arcing plasma balls. Orange ground targets show the locked blast radius and countdown. Rift Warden attempts portal evacuations; CPU Volt Rush approaches reachable allies and tries a rescue dash. As the player, use E or DASH to carry nearby allies beyond the marker before impact.

The robot waits five seconds after loading or rebuilding the city, then opens with its beam cannon, followed by missiles and plasma artillery. Both armies automatically attack the giant robot. Its armor status appears in the scene; choose the Siege Walker camera for a closer view. Click or tap any helicopter, or its PILOT tag, to take first-person flight control. Exit cockpit or press Escape to return to observation.

Hero minimap: the corner radar follows your hero and rotates with the camera. Gold circles show civilian groups and their headcounts; red diamonds mark the Siege Walker and drones. Green H marks evacuation, S marks subway entrances, and cyan dots mark allied heroes. Arrows on the rim point toward units beyond 90 metres. The white arrow points along your view.

Automatic controls: phones and tablets show touch controls. Desktop hides the movement stick and action buttons, showing key reminders instead. Volt Rush uses WASD to move, Space to jump, hold left-click to sustain the primary beam, E for the lightning-wave rescue dash, move the locked mouse to rotate the camera, Shift to boost and Q for overload stun. Mouse movement aims continuously, including while firing with left-click. Right-click has no hero-camera action. Tab opens hero settings and frees the cursor. Escape releases the cursor; click the scene to resume, or press Escape again to exit the hero. Switching input devices clears held controls.

Phone: one finger to orbit, pinch to zoom, two fingers to pan. Arrow buttons raise/lower the camera. Turn your phone sideways for more space.

Desktop: drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom. WASD moves the camera; Q/E changes altitude. Shift moves faster.

Choose a camera preset to follow a tank, helicopter, or infantry soldier. Drag the view to return to free observation. Pause freezes combat and physics while the camera stays available.

Pilot controls: W/S forward/back, A/D strafe, Q/E turn, R/F climb/descend, drag the view or use arrow keys to aim, Space or the FIRE button to launch missiles. Phone: use the movement stick and altitude buttons; drag the scene to aim. You can also hold and drag FIRE to shoot and aim with one thumb. Assisted hover flight stops drifting when you release movement. Pilot mode runs at 1×; pause freezes flight and combat.

Missiles damage the robot as well as buildings, tanks, helicopters, and infantry. Both divisions share the robot as their target and AI fire does not damage allied units. Once the robot is neutralized, they hold fire. Disabled aircraft cannot be piloted. Rebuild city restores the buildings and all units, then restarts the battle. Physics uses rigid building sections, simplified support checks, and a bounded active-debris budget.
